note: Rules and defaults for agentic designs. Thresholds are this tool's configurable defaults, not vendor limits; each rule cites the guidance it follows.

acts.text: It must act in your systems, so designs that only answer (single call, RAG, whole documents, cascade, batch) are ruled out.

steps_known.text: The steps are the same every time, so a fixed workflow is preferred over an autonomous agent: easier to test, cheaper, more predictable.

steps_vary.text: The steps vary per request, so a fixed chain can't cover them; an agent that chooses its next tool is needed.

request_types.text: Requests fall into several distinct types, so routing each type to its own tested handler fits.

single_agent.text: One agent can handle this many tools; add agents only on tool overload or separate domains.

split_agents.text: Many tools or separate specialist domains: an orchestrator with specialist agents keeps each agent's toolset small.

tool_search.text: With this many tools, load tool definitions on demand (tool search) instead of sending all of them on every call.

multi_hop.text: Answers combine several documents or sources, so one retrieval pass is often not enough; agentic retrieval searches again.

retrieval_in_agent.text: The agent both acts and needs your documents, so retrieval becomes one of its tools rather than a separate design.

multi_model_on.text: Different models per role are allowed: cheap models route and check, the stronger model decides.

multi_model_off.text: One model for every role: simpler to operate, evaluate and fail over; designs that need two models are ruled out.

uses_tools.text: It has to search and read as it goes, so designs that answer in one pass without tools are ruled out.

mcp_when: tools are shared across several agents or teams
the vendor already publishes an MCP server
there are many tools to govern in one place
direct_when: one agent uses a few tools
the APIs are internal and change with the agent
controls: Authenticate each MCP server (OAuth or scoped keys), never shared admin credentials
Allow-list the tools each agent may call
Human approval for tools that write, pay or delete
Pin server versions and review tool descriptions on upgrade
Log every tool call with its arguments

retrieval.caveat: This tool doesn't measure retrieval quality yet: test cases include the right passage. Measure search hit rate on your own documents before launch.

chunking.name: Structure-aware chunking
chunking.why: split on headings and sections, a few hundred tokens each, keeping titles with each chunk

hybrid.name: Hybrid search (keyword + vector)
hybrid.why: exact terms like order IDs, product codes and policy names are missed by vector search alone

rerank.name: Reranker
rerank.why: large document sets and a high accuracy target: rerank the top results before answering

filters.name: Metadata filters and document permissions
filters.why: several sources or sensitive data: filter by source, product or date, and only retrieve what the user may see

freshness.name: Incremental re-indexing
freshness.why: documents change often: re-index on change, not on a schedule, and show the document date

citations.name: Citations and a grounding check
citations.why: a wrong answer is costly: every answer cites its passage, unsupported answers are withheld

sql.name: Text-to-SQL over a read-only view
sql.why: the facts live in tables, not documents: query them directly instead of embedding rows

eval.name: Retrieval evaluation
eval.why: measure search hit rate on real questions separately from answer accuracy
